input.reasoning: The graph already holds this claim. The matched node's canonical form, "The Large Hadron Collider poses no danger from microscopic black holes it could produce," states the same proposition as the proposed form: LHC-produced microscopic black holes pose no significant risk. Nothing could bear on one without bearing equally on the other: both decompose identically into whether the LHC can produce black holes, whether they evaporate via Hawking radiation, whether a stable remnant could accrete matter, and whether the cosmic-ray analogy rules out danger. The source's sentence ("no risk of any significance whatsoever from black holes that might be produced at the LHC") asserts exactly this, so the instance affirms. I searched five framings, including two negation forms ("pose a significant risk to Earth"; "could create black holes that destroy the Earth"); no node holds the danger side as a separate claim, so there is no mirror-page risk and no sign the matched node should be inverted. The matched wording is marginally clumsier than the proposed form, but identity does not depend on wording: minting a new node for a better phrasing is exactly the error to avoid, and any wording improvement is the Steward's call on the existing node.
input.relationship_notes: Nearest near-miss: "Collisions at the LHC present no danger" (983da307) is the broader all-risks conclusion (covering strangelets and other scenarios as well), of which the matched black-hole-specific claim is the natural specification; they are distinct claims since different evidence bears on each, but the matched claim plausibly decomposes under it. "The LHC can create microscopic black holes" (6ba67402) is a production premise, not the risk conclusion. "Cosmic-ray collisions in dense stars rule out LHC production of dangerous stable black holes" (8df4a5b0), "Microscopic black holes evaporate essentially instantly through Hawking radiation" (960a19bf), and "Natural cosmic-ray collisions on Earth have already produced the equivalent of the LHC's entire experimental program" (ea8dd956) are evidentiary premises on the safety side. "Quantum-gravity effects near the Planck scale could halt black hole evaporation, leaving a stable remnant" (06c90251) is the premise underlying the contrary risk scenario, and the locus of the live dispute this claim hosts.
